name: Skyways Air Services Ltd
title: Skyways Air Services Ltd - 544890 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue nearly doubled to INR1,216.53 crore on yield and volume, but management attributes much of the jump to fuel-linked pass-through; volume growth 23% is the cited driver with no capacity or capex signal.

summary.headline: Skyways Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores, with consolidated PAT margin at 2.2% versus 1.72%.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27, with operating revenue up 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores and operating EBITDA up to INR50.12 crores from INR27.31 crores. Management attributed much of the revenue jump to per-unit freight cost increases driven by fuel indices, with volume growth of 23% in air cargo and 18% in ocean freight. Employee and other expenses fell as a share of revenue, lifting margins. The company also flagged a board-approved INR30 crore international office expansion and INR20 crore capital infusion into existing overseas subsidiaries, and repaid around INR140 crores of borrowings post-listing.

financial_highlights.metric: Employee benefit expense as % of revenue

financial_highlights.change: absolute increase in quarter; percentage cost reduced per management

segments.name: Air cargo
segments.commentary: Volume growth of 23% YoY; air cargo is about 81% of revenue in Q1 FY27 versus 77% in FY26. Air export volume grew 19% against a market increase of about 3.8%.

segments.name: Ocean freight
segments.commentary: Realisation growth of more than 64% and volume growth of 18% YoY; management cited revenue growth of 63%.

segments.name: Express
segments.commentary: Revenue up 64% YoY to INR63 crores, with 59,700 shipments across 31 locations.

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (Odyssey)
segments.commentary: Pharma was 8-9% of business before Odyssey and reached 23% last year. Odyssey standalone revenue rose from about INR130 crores to INR182 crores quarter-on-quarter.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance; management will give volume guidance each quarter with the earnings call.
Management expects volume growth trend to continue in Q2 FY27 and says Q2 operating performance is improving QoQ.
Board approved INR30 crores for five new Asian international offices; breakeven at EBITDA level expected in 15-18 months and at PAT level in 2-3 years.
Generic group capex of about INR35-40 crores per year; cold chain warehouse expected to be operational next quarter.
Digital booking platform (ASAP) expected to launch within 30-60 days.
capex_capacity: Board approved INR30 crores for international office expansion; management said about 15% is capex and the rest is setup cost and working capital.
INR20 crores incremental capital infusion approved for existing overseas subsidiaries in UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam.
Generic group capex of INR35-40 crores per annum, including warehouses and offices.
Cold chain warehouse project to become operational in the next quarter.
No acquisitions approved beyond the INR30 crore and INR20 crore allocations; management prefers organic growth.
demand_pricing: Management attributes about 23-25% of revenue growth to volume and the balance to higher per-unit freight cost driven by fuel indices; Brent-linked fuel index rose from about USD61/barrel in January to about USD110/barrel in May.
Management says fuel surcharges are a full pass-through, and yield moves up or down with fuel indices.
Air yield rose to about 416 from 259 in Q1 FY26 (per management).
Company ranked number one air freight forwarder in India and 44th globally by WorldACD chargeable volumes; Indian market share rose from 5.9% to 6.2% QoQ.
West Asia disruption reduced airline capacity by about 20%; management said it secured alternate carrier capacity and gained new customers.
Sector strength cited: pharmaceuticals, textiles and readymade garments, automotive, consumer electronics; no non-veg handling.
Indian air export market rose about 3.8% to about 3.06 lakh metric tons in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state revenue run rate, given revenue has roughly doubled YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 23-25% of revenue growth came from volume and the rest from per-unit cost increases driven by fuel indices; it did not give a steady-state figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% volume growth sustainable, and is the realisation growth tied to fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of sustaining volume growth and aims to improve it; yield is market-driven and fuel is a pass-through. Focus is on higher-yield trade lanes.

qa_highlights.question: Gestation period and capex for new Asian offices?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical gestation is 2-4 years; management targets 2-3 years. About 15% of the INR30 crores is capex. Current footprint covers Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Bangladesh.

qa_highlights.question: Which markets get the INR20 crore subsidiary infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the digital booking platform?
qa_highlights.answer: Air, ocean and express are in pilot; trucking is in final development. Launch expected in 30-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the EOW matter in the prospectus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub judice and under investigation in final stages, and it sees no financial impact at present. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the post-listing debt repayment and capital raise drag ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said historical ROE is 14-15%, the September quarter will show the post-listing capital effect, and it targets around 15% over time. About INR140 crores of borrowings were repaid.

risks_watch: Revenue growth is largely price-driven by fuel indices; management says yield can fall if crude declines.
Margin sustainability: management has chosen to absorb some cost increases to stay customer-centric, and gross margin percentage may be affected.
Pending EOW investigation: management says the matter is sub judice with no timeline and no expected financial impact.
Finance cost rose in absolute terms to INR17.7 crores; debt repayment benefit is expected from Q3 and Q4.
ROE may dilute temporarily after the post-listing equity increase and debt repayment, per management.
Swissport bid was not successful; company is now bidding with a Swissport alliance.
Brace Port (listed subsidiary) share price has declined since listing; management declined to comment on the stock price.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes and market share, but evasive on steady-state revenue, yield and multi-year targets, which management repeatedly deferred to fuel-index dynamics. Cautious on the EOW matter and on ROE, where it gave no quantitative answer for Q1.
key_quotes: The whole bucket of the way you look at the revenue, almost 23% to 25% of that comes through the volumes, and the rest is coming through the increase in the per-unit cost for the logistics.
The fuel cost is always a pass-through for us.
So, the matter is still sub judice and under investigation in its final stages.
The ROE historically has been 14% to 15%, and we would have, as the capital base has gone increased in the in the in the month of September post-listing, the capital increase.

Once the war situation comes to a little control, we see a huge amount of opportunity in the Middle East for the organization to expand its solutions because there will be a lot of infrastructure build-up that will be required in that region.

adds.what: INR30 crore board-approved expansion for five new Asian international offices

growth.why: No revenue guidance is given; management expects the volume growth trend to continue into Q2 FY27, backed by a board-approved INR30 crore office expansion, a cold chain warehouse due next quarter, and secured alternate carrier capacity, while about three-quarters of the 90% revenue jump came from higher fuel-linked freight rates rather than volume.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Employee expense fell to 2.94% of revenue from 4.41% and other expenses to 1.76% from 2.5%, lifting PAT margin to 2.2% from 1.72%, but management said it is absorbing some cost increases to stay customer-centric and gross margin % may be affected, and yield falls if crude declines.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: next 1 quarter for cold chain; 15-18 months to EBITDA breake
rows.why: Cold chain warehouse is expected operational next quarter and the board approved INR30 crore for five new Asian offices, with management targeting 2-3 years gestation, though the offices are small (about INR4.5 crore of capex, per the brief's growth read).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Air cargo volume grew 23% YoY and ocean 18%, management expects the trend to continue into Q2 FY27, and Indian air export market share rose from 5.9% to 6.2% QoQ, though the market itself grew only about 3.8%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Generic group capex is guided at INR35-40 crore per annum and INR20 crore subsidiary infusion is approved, but no utilisation figure was disclosed, so a fresh capex round cannot be firmly called.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue guidance is given; management expects volume growth to continue into Q2 FY27 (volume up 23% in air cargo and 18% in ocean) and Q2 operating performance is improving QoQ, but the 90% revenue jump is about three-quarters price-driven and not guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Yield is market-driven and fuel-linked, and management said yield can fall if crude declines (Brent-linked index went from about USD61 in January to about USD110 in May), with finance cost already up to INR17.7 crore and ROE expected to dilute after the post-listing capital raise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: within 30-60 days (ASAP digital booking platform); cold chai
rows.why: Digital booking platform (ASAP) is in pilot for air, ocean and express with trucking in final development, and management guided a launch in 30-60 days.

rows.label: Alternate carrier capacity after West Asia disruption
rows.why: West Asia disruption cut airline capacity by about 20%, management secured alternate carrier capacity and gained new customers, supporting volume share gains.

rows.label: Debt repayment benefit on finance cost
rows.why: About INR140 crore of borrowings were repaid post-listing and management expects the finance cost benefit from Q3 and Q4, though Q1 finance cost rose to INR17.7 crore in absolute terms.

rows.label: EOW investigation (sub judice)
rows.why: Management says the matter is in final investigation stages with no financial impact seen currently and no timeline, so it remains an open legal overhang.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth and market share (air export volume +19% vs market +3.8%) but evasive on steady-state revenue, yield and multi-year targets, deferring to fuel-index dynamics; analysts pushed on sustainability of 25-30% volume growth, fuel linkage of realisation, and the ROE
